correctness.rationale: Finite universal quantifiers are certified exhaustively: every n-tree is obtained by leaf attachment from n−1 and all duplicates eliminated by a rooted-tree canonical string, with induction proving completeness. All 749 tree-root pairs up to n=9 have determinants independently computed by fraction-free elimination and exact rational elimination; the resulting frequency counts and unique order-nine shape are asserted. A direct mod-two left-null witness together with determinant index two proves the complete parity target restriction and Cayley–Hamilton extends it to all horizons. No infinite extrapolation is claimed.

value.rationale: A sharp smallest-order counterexample settles a motivated boundary: real controllability and integer exact-state reachability coincide for every controllable unweighted tree with at most eight vertices, but can diverge at nine. The unique unrooted witness and exact parity constraint identify a concrete lattice obstruction, relevant when actuator commands and targets must be integers. This is a natural complete small-order classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or restatement of real rank.
